# Basic coding
Having basics in math and statistics is a prerequisite in for data-dealing scientists. This has been the norm for a while. These topics have been part of the curriculum for a while. Not that field biologist will not complain by that.  Data analyses were done with SPSS, STATA, and also EXCEL STAT. The rise of R  introduced a new paradigm on how to analyses data and visualize data. There are many benefit: it is free and it faciliate reproducibility, it keeps growing. The catch is that  is that unlike the softwares above, it is a programming language. And unlike stat and math, to the best of my knowledge, programing is not engrained in the curriculum.

Learning a programming language R is mostly unlearning how to use a computer.
With mouse, touchscreen, and even vocal commands (speech to text), using keyboard is almost obsolete.
In fact, especially with AI, interacting with a computer is more and more like interacting with human.
Monetary succes is not necessarily on practical but how friendly interface, easy of use.
At the other end, we have those prgramming language were friendliness is not the main concerns.

There are over 8,945 programming languages recorded in the Online Historical Encyclopaedia of Programming Languages (HOPL).
About 50-70 are actually actively used like C, phyton etc.
Some are experimental or just for fun.
Like, once you understand the basic, it is easier to go from one language to another.
Because it is based on the same principle.
R is one of those, and while we will look at R, I will do the best to look at the big picture. So hopefully about programing language.

This is divided into three main themes: the environment where one works with (@sec-console and @sec-script, and @sec-ide), the atomic or elementary objects: numeric (@sec-numeric), strings (@sec-character) and boolean (@sec-boolean). The data object which are  vector @sec-vector, matrix @sec-matrixCoding, data frame @sec-dataframe and list @sec-list. Mirroring math concept on arithmetic and matrix operation equivalent @sec-arithmeticCoding @sec-matrixOperationCoding and @sec-matrixMultiplicationCoding @sec-booleanOperationCoding The last part is function in R program. Once these is just finding which function you need.
